overview: A third of the positions are in media and content, and marketing is next. Out of 74 positions there is one data analyst and one agent, even though data analysis and NIL are both on the class's own list of jobs that will grow.

The case for a human over AI is nearly the same everywhere: AI can't feel and it can't connect. 21 of 74 answers name emotion, empathy or feelings, and 26 name connection, relationships or trust. None of the 73 skills answers lists using AI as a skill.

Some of the "AI can't" claims are already out of date. "AI cannot cook" and "AI cannot physically manage a field" sit next to a world where robots paint the lines on athletic fields and work restaurant fryers. The stronger answers give the numbers to AI and argue for judgment, like the scout who watches how a player responds after a mistake.

The predictions agree on what fades: stat tracking (13 of 24) and ticketing (8). What rises is content (11) and the people who build the tech (10). Many named their own field as fading, and only one of 23 answers about the industry mentions streaming, the week the NFL is on Netflix.
Worktopia offered everyone a horrible job first. 13 turned it down on the spot, 12 took at least one, and one person accepted 23 before saying no. The game scored an average of 4.6 stars.

sections.label: What value will this position provide to the sports ecosystem in 2034?
sections.summary: Fans are the most common answer, and keeping sports human is the most common argument. Eleven answers name the money: revenue, sponsors, sales.

themes.note: Bringing fans in, keeping them, connecting them to athletes.

As AI becomes more intelligent, it is up to the head coach to make sure that the AI is supporting players, not taking away from the human competition.
This position will make more people interested in watching sports at home and that would mean media services will get more sponsorships which leads to more money.

sections.gaps: Many of them named their own field. Media and content are a third of the positions, and here seven name editing, highlights or cameras as fading and three name broadcasting. One student said it outright and picked sports journalist anyway, as a kind of activism. That is the question worth putting to every media pick: what part of the job is still yours in 2034?

sections.label: Which jobs will be much more popular?

sections.gaps: Data is on both lists, and read closely the answers agree: the stat tracker fades and the analyst rises. Four named NIL, agents or athlete branding as growing, and one student out of 25 picked agent as a position.

sections.label: Please review Worktopia.
sections.summary: 25 people gave stars, an average of 4.6: 16 fives, 7 fours and 2 threes. Most of the written reviews say it felt like a game instead of an assignment.

themes.theme: Fun, and not like an assignment
examples: This was SO cool!!! Genuinely felt like a real interactive game while completing an assignment. Such a cool idea!

sections.gaps: Two fixes were asked for: a spell checker, and less of the green scan line. One review found the whole thing a bit depressing, which is a fair read of the premise.
